prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Denver. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you targeted practice names — but to avoid giving stale or incorrect local listings I need your ZIP code or neighborhood in Denver (so I can tailor recommendations by proximity, insurance acceptance, and whether you want a low-cost school clinic vs private practice). Want me to look up current, nearby offices?

Meanwhile, here are the specific types of practices you should call and why — plus exactly what to ask each one when you call. This will get you the best options for a dental implant in Denver.

Which specific offices to call (by type)
- An oral & maxillofacial surgery (OMS) practice — why: OMS surgeons place implants, handle extractions, bone grafts and complex cases, and offer IV sedation/general anesthesia. Good for medically complex or multiple-implant cases.
- A periodontist who places implants — why: periodontists specialize in gum and bone health and are excellent for implants where periodontal disease or bone grafting is involved.
- A prosthodontist or a restorative dentist experienced in implant restorations — why: they design and place the final crowns, bridges, or full-arch prostheses; coordination between surgeon and restorative dentist is crucial for a good long-term result.
- An implant specialty center that offers both surgery and restoration in-house — why: seamless communication, fewer handoffs, often digital planning and same-day provisional options.
- University dental clinic (University of Colorado School of Dental Medicine) — why: lower-cost supervised care by faculty and senior students; good option if budget is important.

How to find specific Denver practices right now
- Use these directories and filters to find high-quality clinicians in Denver:
  - American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) “Find an Implant Dentist”
  - American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS) “Find a Surgeon”
  - American Academy of Periodontology (AAP) “Find a Periodontist”
  - American College of Prosthodontists (ACP) “Find a Prosthodontist”
  - Colorado Dental Association and local Google Maps (check reviews)
- Call the University of Colorado dental clinic for supervised implant care and pricing.

What to ask when you call (ask all practices)
- How many implants do you place per year and how many similar cases have you done? (experience)
- Do you place implants and do the restorative crowns/bridges here or refer out? (coordination)
- Will you use a CBCT scan and digital planning/prosthetic-driven placement? (diagnostics/planning)
- What implant systems/brands do you use and what warranty/aftercare is provided? (materials)
- Do you do bone grafts/sinus lifts here if needed? How often? (complexity)
- What sedation/anesthesia options are available? (comfort)
- Rough estimate of total cost (surgery + implant + abutment + crown) and financing options; do you accept my insurance? (cost)
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references or reviews? (outcomes)
- Expected timeline from surgery to final crown and typical follow-up schedule. (timing)
- What happens if the implant fails within the first year? (guarantee/repair policy)

If you want, tell me:
- Your Denver neighborhood or ZIP code
- Whether you have dental insurance and any medical issues (e.g., diabetes, smoking) or teeth that need extraction
- Whether you want lowest cost, fastest timeline (same-day), or highest-specialist care

I’ll return a short list (3–6 specific Denver practices—oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist/implant center, and the university clinic) and a one-line reason to call each. Which ZIP or neighborhood should I use?
